newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower after rate hike.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower after rate hike.

text.p: New York precious metals ended lower after early weakness in palladium and silver, later spread to platinum and gold, and the latter was dragged down further following news of a 0.25 percent rate hike which pushed the yellow metal to its low for the day, traders said.

"The interest rate factor, although discounted and talked about, is certainly not bullish," William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said. "Rate hikes in the current non-overly inflationary atmosphere are just not psychologically good, and there is an opportunity lost with higher interest rates for metals."
COMEX June gold ended $2.50 weaker at $350.50 an ounce.
Bullion was quoted at $347.30/$347.80 an ounce, down from $349.35/85 just after the over-the-counter options expired at 0930 EST.
Palladium, despite losses Monday and Tuesday, was still seen as overpriced by some analysts and dealers.

The white metal rode high on the back of Russian supply concerns, but those have eased as the likelihood of resumption of deliveries to Japan neared, and the threat of a strike at Norilsk in Russia has been put back until at least June 30 by the labor unions, traders noted.
NYMEX June palladium ended $2.45 weaker at $146.80.
New York palladium, to a great extent, was falling in line with Zurich and London which saw heavy selling overnight, dealers said.
"If we go below $140 in palladium, good short covering will come in from Tokyo speculative futures people. There is a huge short there," a pgm dealer said.
NYMEX April platinum went out $3.00 weaker at $375.50 an ounce, traded $379.50 to $374.50.
Although many now saw platinum as fairly priced, it could be open to a downward adjustment because the platinum premium over gold has widened so much, analysts cautioned.
COMEX silver tumbled on speculative liquidation which hit sell stops as funds moved in to sell, traders said. No fresh fundamental reason was cited.
COMEX May silver settled 7.7 cents weaker at $5.12 an ounce, traded $5.195 to $5.10.
Palladium, and to some extent silver, had helped to prop up gold recently, but weakness in both accelerated the decline in the yellow metal Tuesday, traders said.
Volume in COMEX gold was relatively heavy at an estimated 80,000 lots, but there were 18,803 switches as the rollover from April to June continued. June has become most-actively traded.
COMEX silver volume was estimated at 19,000 lots.

But Merrill Lynch's O'Neill was concerned that although the market may well have discounted Tuesday's rate hike by the Federal Reserve, other increases may be in the pipeline because "the central bank rarely acts once".
